title: A Moment Apart
blurb: Widescreen electronic pop built from choirs, field recordings and enormous drums. The duo's breakout festival record.

title: The Last Goodbye
blurb: Built around sampled gospel and soul recordings, stitched into something warmer and more nostalgic than its predecessor.

title: When Will We Land?
blurb: A debut that wanders from piano house to broken beat without ever losing its footing on the dance floor.

title: Kingdoms in Colour
blurb: Travel notes turned into music: dusty percussion, live bass and vocals that drift in and back out again.

title: Hallucinating Love
blurb: A patient return after seven years away, leaning further into songwriting while keeping the loose, hazy grooves.

title: Cold Enough for Snow
blurb: Long, patient builds and glassy synth lines. Made for headphones on a late train as much as for a club.

title: Isles
blurb: Rave nostalgia rebuilt as something you can listen to sitting down, all breakbeats and wordless vocal hooks.

title: Brightest Lights
blurb: Seventy minutes of steady, melodic deep house from a producer known for phones-away shows.

title: Fragments
blurb: Assembled slowly out of small pieces during a year of enforced stillness, then opened up into something communal.

title: Solace
blurb: Cavernous, slow-burning house with live drums and vocals pitched somewhere between a ballad and a club track.

title: Good Lies
blurb: Two brothers chopping vocal samples into garage and breaks. Sharp, bright, and over before it outstays its welcome.

title: Cascade
blurb: A producer with a neuroscience doctorate turning club tracks into something closer to chamber music.
